paragraphs: Anyone looking for a fostering agency in Newham can choose between the council's own fostering service and the independent agencies on this page. The council recruits and supports carers for Newham's own children; an agency approves and supervises its carers itself and is asked by councils, Newham among them, when a child needs a home. Newham's children's services were judged outstanding in every area by Ofsted, announced in January 2026, and the council quotes the inspectors' finding that its foster carers receive excellent support.

The council's sufficiency strategy for 2022 to 2025 shows why it wants more local carers. At the end of March 2022, 155 of the 361 children in its care lived with independent agency carers and 96 with council carers, and the strategy set the aim of a much larger share of foster homes provided in house, with carers from a wide range of ethnic backgrounds and homes for disabled children, teenagers including young people seeking asylum, emergencies and short breaks. Its July 2026 campaign, "Be the missing piece", said the council still has to rely on agencies to find homes quickly and asked in particular for carers from the borough's Bangladeshi and Black African communities, including Somali, Nigerian and Ghanaian families.

The children waiting range from babies and toddlers to teenagers, many of whom stay with one carer until they are ready to live on their own. There are also brothers and sisters to keep together, young parents who move in with their baby, and children with disabilities or who have been through complex trauma. A separate specialist scheme looks for people with childcare, education, health or family experience of additional needs, often for children leaving residential care, with three weeks of respite a year, weekly social work visits and the council's own clinical team.

To apply to the council you need to be over 21, live within reasonable travelling distance of Newham and have room for a child, whether you rent or own; you can be single or in a couple, working or at home. Council carers have their own social worker, a 24-hour line, a monthly support group, the Newham Foster Carers' Association, free Fostering Network membership, Mockingbird and full Council Tax exemption. We do not have a Newham allowance page yet, so ask the council and each agency for its weekly rates in writing.

The council runs online information sessions and library drop-ins. Families on the borough's borders can also look at the Tower Hamlets, Hackney, Waltham Forest, Barking and Dagenham and London pages.
